title: AERO9500 Final Report (Part 2) – Space Mission Design
overview: Students design a preliminary space mission benefiting Australia, covering the space segment: mission purpose, spacecraft count, users, launch site and vehicle, orbit and orbital elements, manoeuvres, ground control and communications, mission duration and end-of-life. Design may use STK, PIGI or approved software, supplemented by hand calculations, and is reported as a concise technical report with supporting screenshots and software files.
deliverables: Single PDF technical report submitted via Turnitin on Moodle
Relevant screenshots included in the report or appendix
All relevant STK or PIGI (or other approved) software files included with the report or in the appendix

format.length: Maximum 20 pages for the core part, excluding title page, table of contents, references, etc.
format.structure: Executive summary; Introduction (mission overview and rationale); Main body covering all space segment sections (e.g. launch, orbit, ground stations, coverage, mission operation, end-of-life); Conclusion; Bibliography. Figures and tables fully and correctly labelled (figure number, title, reference if necessary).
format.other: Clear, effective engineering-report writing style with correct grammar and spelling; clear and logical overall structure; all non-original text, diagrams and ideas clearly identified and properly cited and referenced; Wikipedia not accepted as a proper source; report checked for plagiarism.

requirements.text: Design a space mission that benefits Australia in some way, keeping the mission concept simple (e.g. bushfire tracking/alert, weather satellite, internet/communication, Earth observation for city planning/real estate).
Identify and describe the main elements of the mission's space segment.
State whether one or multiple spacecraft will be used.
Identify the users, including the operator and customers.
Specify the launch site and the launch vehicle.
Specify the orbit type and its characteristics and orbital elements.
Identify the ground control facilities to be used and state how often the spacecraft can communicate with ground control.
State the mission duration and the plans for end-of-life (EOL).

Complete the design using software of choice (STK, PIGI, or other software such as flightclub only after contacting Naomi to discuss), supplementing with hand calculations as needed; if using PIGI, register for the competition to obtain a licence.
Include relevant screenshots and all relevant STK or PIGI files with the report or in the appendix.
Produce the report as a single PDF document with the required sections: executive summary, introduction, main body, conclusion, bibliography.
Fully and correctly label all figures and tables (figure number, title, and reference if necessary).
Clearly identify and properly cite and reference all text, diagrams, ideas or other information not originating with the student; do not use Wikipedia as a proper source.
